turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_train.csv: 300 real steels, process/composition
    columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B, Al, Cu, W, S, Heat treatment
    step 1 temperature, Heat treatment step 1 time, Heat treatment step 1 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 2
    temperature, Heat treatment step 2 time, Heat treatment step 2 cooling rate, Heat treatment step 3
    temperature, Heat treatment step 3 time, Heat treatment step 3 cooling rate, Secondary treatment step 1
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 1 time, Secondary treatment step 2 temperature, Secondary treatment step 2
    time, Secondary treatment step 3 temperature, Secondary treatment step 3 time, Secondary treatment step 4
    temperature, Secondary treatment step 4 time, Thermal exposure temperature, Thermal exposure time) and
    the two measured objectives `yield strength (MPa)` and `elongation (%)`
    (both at room temperature).
  - b3_htsteel_pareto_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE steels whose objectives were
    NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and the same process/composition
    columns.

Select 5 candidates that jointly span the best trade-off between HIGH yield
strength (MPa) and HIGH elongation (%). Neither objective is given for the
pool. Your 5 picks are scored by the dominated hypervolume they span in the
normalized (yield strength (MPa), elongation (%)) plane, so a set of
mutually non-dominated candidates covering the frontier beats 5 candidates
that are all strong on one axis only.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit list of
candidate_ids, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Reasoning

**Step 1 — Learn the training frontier.** The training Pareto front (high YS, high elongation) runs roughly through:
- (206 MPa, 80%), (290 MPa, 78%) — solution-annealed austenitics
- (375 MPa, 53%), (440 MPa, 50%) — high-Si / Cr-Ni austenitics
- (700 MPa, 34%), (1000 MPa, 25%) — high-Ti γ'-strengthened Ni-rich steels
- (1300 MPa, 19%), (1380 MPa, 15%) — tempered 11–13Cr martensitics
- (1578 MPa, 7.8%), (1900 MPa, 8%) — PH/maraging extremes

**Step 2 — Match pool candidates to near-identical training rows.**

- **c018** (18Cr–8.75Ni–0.4Ti, 1050 °C/1 h + 700 °C/20 h): exact training match gave **278 MPa, 62%** — the most reliable high-ductility pick in the pool (mild 600 °C aging should keep ~280–310 MPa, ~55–60%).
- **c016** (20.5Cr–13.5Ni–2.5Si, 1125 °C/0.5 h solution): near-duplicate of the training row 62.37Fe/20.5Cr/13.5Ni/2.5Si at 1150 °C → **375 MPa, 53%** — an excellent knee point.
- **c012** (11.25Cr–19.5Ni–2.9Ti, solution + AH 750 °C/16 h): identical composition trained at 1050 °C + 700 °C/3 h gave **700 MPa, 34%**; the stronger age here should give ~700–780 MPa, ~28–34% — mid-frontier.
- **c056** (11.25Cr–23Ni–2.9Ti, 1120 °C/4 h + AH 735 °C/16 h): identical composition with double-age gave **1000 MPa, 25%**; this route should land ~800–1000 MPa at ~25% — upper-mid frontier.
- **c053** (11.25Cr–1.65Ni–1.8W martensitic, tempered at 450 °C): the close sibling composition tempered at 450 °C gave **1380 MPa, 15%** — the strength anchor (its own composition tempered at 650 °C gave 750 MPa/16%, so the low temper drives it to ~1300–1400 MPa while keeping ~13–15%).

Alternatives like c057 (~1100 MPa, 13%), c034 (uncertain 900–1400 MPa, low ductility), c042/c046 (dominated by c016/c018 estimates) add less hypervolume.

**Step 3 — Coverage check.** Predicted set: (≈290, 60), (≈375, 53), (≈720, 32), (≈950, 25), (≈1350, 15) — mutually non-dominated and spanning the full frontier from ductile to ultra-strong.

Final: c018, c016, c012, c056, c053
